chunks: Mu‘āwiyah ibn ‘Ammār narrated from Abī ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Whoever reaches Jam‘ has indeed attained the hajj."
And he said: "Any qārin, mufrid, or mutamatti‘ who arrives after the hajj has passed him by, then let him exit ihram with an ‘umrah, and hajj is due upon him the following year."

He said: And he said regarding a man who reaches the Imam while he is at Jam‘: "If he thinks that he can go to ‘Arafāt and stand there for a short while, then reach Jam‘ before sunrise, then he should go to it. But if he thinks that he will not reach it until they have departed, then he should not go to it, and his hajj has been completed."

key_terms.الْحَجَّ: the hajj pilgrimage being discussed in terms of validity or being missed
key_terms.بِعُمْرَةٍ: with an ‘umrah, by which the pilgrim exits the state after missing hajj
key_terms.جَمْعًا: Jam‘, meaning Muzdalifah, the sacred site relevant to the validity of hajj rites
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: sunrise, the time limit mentioned for returning to Jam‘
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: ‘Arafāt, the place of standing during hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who reaches Jam‘ or misses the hajj during pilgrimage?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning one who reaches Jam‘ during hajj and one who misses the standing connected with hajj. It explains that reaching Jam‘ counts toward attaining the hajj, while one who has missed hajj must complete with an ‘umrah and perform hajj again the following year. It also gives a practical ruling for someone at Jam‘ who may still be able to reach ‘Arafāt briefly and return before sunrise.
